title: One-step dimension-reducing Cohen--Macaulay groupoid slice
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], all structure morphisms being over $S$. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $x\in X$ if it is flat at $x$ (the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$) [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the local ring at $x$ of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_{f(x)}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equal to Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. It is Cohen--Macaulay if this holds at every point. Assume $s,t$ are Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $u\in U$ be a finite type point, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $F_u=R\times_{s,U}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ and $G_u=R\times_{(s,t),U\times_SU,(u,u)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Set $d_1=\dim G_u$ and $d_2=\dim_{e(u)}F_u$, where global dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and dimension at a point is the minimum of dimensions of open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. If $d_2$ is finite and $d_2>d_1$, there exist an affine scheme $B$, a locally finitely presented immersion $g:B\to U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $b\in B$ with $g(b)=u$ and $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(b)$ an isomorphism, such that the morphism $h=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:B\times_{g,U,t}R\to U$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $x=(b,e(u))$. For the restricted groupoid with arrow scheme $R_B=B\times_{g,U,t}R\times_{s,U,g}B$ and source $s_B:R_B\to B$ the last projection, one has $\dim_{e_B(b)}(s_B^{-1}(b))=d_2-1$, where $e_B(b)=(b,e(u),b)$.

source.place: Tag 0461 (lemma-slice), all conclusions, and Tag 04MY (situation-slice). The immersion identifies the point and its residue field; the finite-dimension hypothesis is explicit here.

proof.text: Apply the field-point criterion to the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $u$ in which $u$ is closed, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Write $k=A/\mathfrak m=\kappa(u)$. Choose an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}D$ containing $e(u)$ inside $s^{-1}(V)\cap t^{-1}(V)$, and let $\mathfrak q$ represent $e(u)$. Both maps $s,t:A\to D$ contract $\mathfrak q$ to $\mathfrak m$. Their residue maps $k\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ are the same isomorphism: the map induced by $e$ is a common inverse, since $se=te=1$. In particular $e(u)$ is a $k$-rational point of $F_u$.

source.place: Tag 0461 (lemma-slice), proof, first paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 01TA (lemma-point-finite-type).

proof.text: Put $T=\mathcal O_{R,e(u)}=D_{\mathfrak q}$ and $C=T/s(\mathfrak m)T$. The fibre-stalk quotient identifies $C$ with $\mathcal O_{F_u,e(u)}$. By hypothesis it is a nonzero Noetherian local Cohen--Macaulay ring. Its Krull dimension is $d_2$: base change of the locally finite type map $s$ gives a locally finite type $k$-scheme $F_u$; choose a finite-type affine neighbourhood of $e(u)$ in it and apply the field dimension formula. Its transcendence-degree term is zero by Step 1, and passing to an open neighbourhood leaves both the stalk and dimension at the point unchanged.

source.place: Tag 0461 (lemma-slice), first paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 02FX (lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point); schemes.tex Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre).

proof.text: Form the restricted groupoid on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with arrow scheme $H=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{u,U,t}R\times_{s,U,u}\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its operations are obtained componentwise from those of $R$; the groupoid equations remain the same equations after pullback. Its source and target are locally of finite type. Indeed their factors are base changes of $s,t$ and of $u:\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$, using the cited base-change lemma. Their composites are locally of finite type: on affine charts a composite of two finitely generated algebras is generated by the union of the two finite lists of generators. Its stabilizer is $G_u$: on test schemes both specify an arrow with its two endpoints equal to the same given $k$-point. Regard these schemes as algebraic spaces by their representable sheaves. The two field-groupoid dimension statements, using the identity scheme charts, give $\dim_{e_H}H=\dim H=\dim G_u=d_1$.

source.place: Tag 0461 (lemma-slice), second paragraph; Tags 04MP, 04ML, 04MQ, 04LU; spaces-more-groupoids.tex Tags 06FF and 06FD, specialized to schemes.

proof.text: The point $e_H$ is $k$-rational. The part of $H$ lying over $W$ is affine and of finite type over $k$: it is a closed subscheme of the affine part of the $s$-fibre, whose coordinate algebra is finitely generated over $k$. Apply the field dimension formula on a finite-type affine neighbourhood in $H$, obtaining $\dim\mathcal O_{H,e_H}=d_1$. Compute its local ring by taking first the $s$-fibre and then the $t$-fibre at $u$. On the affine neighbourhood $W$, $u\to V$ is the closed immersion defined by $\mathfrak m$. The affine pullback formula gives the coordinate quotient $D/(s(\mathfrak m)D+t(\mathfrak m)D)$, and localization at the identity gives $\mathcal O_{H,e_H}=T/(s(\mathfrak m)T+t(\mathfrak m)T)=C/J$, where $J$ is the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak m$ under $A\xrightarrow t T\to C$. Thus $\dim(C/J)=d_1<d_2$. These are two endpoint conditions, not the single stabilizer equation $s=t$ on arbitrary field-valued endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0461 (lemma-slice), third paragraph, affine quotient for the restriction; morphisms.tex Tag 02FX; schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes).

proof.text: The associated primes $P_1,\ldots,P_r$ of the self-module $C$ form a finite set. For each $P_j$, the depth bound gives $\dim(C/P_j)\ge\operatorname{depth}C=d_2$. The ideal $J$ is not contained in $P_j$: otherwise $C/P_j$ is a quotient of $C/J$, and lifting prime chains along the quotient would give $\dim(C/P_j)\le d_1$, a contradiction. Let $Q_j$ be the inverse image of $P_j$ under $A\xrightarrow t T\to C$. These are prime ideals and $\mathfrak m\not\subseteq Q_j$. Prime avoidance supplies $f\in\mathfrak m$ outside all $Q_j$. If the associated-prime list were empty the zerodivisor theorem would make $0$ a nonzerodivisor on the nonzero ring $C$, which is impossible; thus the nonempty-list version applies. Set $a=t(f)\in T$. Its image $\bar a\in C$ lies in no associated prime, so the zerodivisor theorem makes multiplication by $\bar a$ injective. Also $a$ and $\bar a$ lie in the respective maximal ideals because $f\in\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tags 00DS (lemma-silly), 0BK4 (lemma-depth-dim-associated-primes), 00LD (lemma-ass-zero-divisors), and 00LC (lemma-finite-ass); implements the prime-avoidance paragraph of Tag 0461 using associated primes directly.

proof.text: Define $B=\operatorname{Spec}(A/(f))$ and $g:B\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow U$. The first map is the closed immersion defined by the principal ideal $(f)$, so $g$ is an immersion. It is locally of finite presentation directly from the presentation $A/(f)$ with one relation and no algebra generators, followed by an open immersion, which is locally of finite presentation. Let $b$ be the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/(f)$. Then $g(b)=u$ and the induced residue map identifies $\kappa(b)=(A/(f))/(\mathfrak m/(f))=A/\mathfrak m=k$.

source.place: Tag 0461 (lemma-slice), paragraph beginning Set A prime = A/fA: conclusions (1)--(3).

proof.text: The affine pullback formula identifies the part of $B\times_{g,U,t}R$ lying over $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(D/(t(f)))$. Hence its local ring at $x=(b,e(u))$ is $T/aT$ and the map from $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ is induced by $s$. To prove this map flat without a Noetherian hypothesis on $U$, apply the existing fibre-regular slicing lemma to $s:R\to U$ at $e(u)$ and the one-element germ $a=t(f)$. Step 5 makes this singleton a regular sequence in its fibre ring $C$ (it is a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal). The lemma supplies a local cut, flat over $U$, by a section with this very germ. Its stalk map is exactly $\mathcal O_{U,u}\to T/aT$. Thus $h$ is flat at $x$, irrespective of whether the neighbourhood supplied by that lemma equals our original $W$.

source.place: Tag 0461 (lemma-slice), flatness paragraph; more-morphisms.tex Tag 06LI (lemma-slice-given-elements), r=1, whose one-element case is Tag 056Y (lemma-slice-given-element).

proof.text: The fibre-stalk quotient applied to $h$ gives $\mathcal O_{h^{-1}(u),x}=(T/aT)/s(\mathfrak m)(T/aT)=C/(\bar a)$. The Cohen--Macaulay nonzerodivisor quotient theorem says this is Noetherian local of dimension $d_2-1$ and depth at least $d_2-1$. Its depth is also at most its dimension by the depth--support bound applied to its nonzero self-module (whose support is the whole prime spectrum). Thus depth equals dimension. Together with Step 7 this proves that $h$ is Cohen--Macaulay at $x$.

source.place: Tag 0461 (lemma-slice), Cohen--Macaulay quotient paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM) and 00LK (lemma-bound-depth).

proof.text: Finally $s_B^{-1}(b)\cong h^{-1}(u)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$ by associating the fibre products in $R_B=B\times_{g,U,t}R\times_{s,U,g}B$. Step 6 makes the latter field base change the identity, and sends $e_B(b)$ to $x$. Near this point the fibre has affine equation $t(f)=0$ in the finite-type $k$-scheme $F_u$, so it has a finite-type affine neighbourhood. The field dimension formula has zero transcendence-degree term because the point has residue field $k$. Its topological dimension at the point therefore equals the local-ring dimension from Step 8, namely $d_2-1$. This is precisely the remaining assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q49-6609a00fa (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 20 cited node statements and Stacks more-groupoids 04MY/0461 with its full proof. The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged from Q101's creation. There are no new nodes. The nine steps follow 0461. Step 1: the 01TA/02J2 node gives an affine V in which u is closed; the residue maps agree via e. Step 2: fibre-stalk quotient plus 02FX at a rational point gives dim C = d2. Step 3: the restricted groupoid H has stabilizer G_u (04ML, checked on fibre products); the 04LU and 04MQ nodes, via the identity chart, give dim H = d1. Step 4: the affine pullback gives O_{H,e} = C/J with dim d1. Step 5: associated-prime avoidance (00LC, 0BK4, 00DS, 00LD) replaces the source's minimal primes. It is valid: J not in any P_j because dim C/P_j >= d2 > d1; the empty Ass case is excluded. Step 6: B = Spec A/(f) is an lfp immersion with kappa(b) = k. Step 7: flatness comes from the same-unit 056Y slice node applied to s with germ t(f), with no Noetherian base. Step 8: the CM quotient node plus depth <= dim. Step 9: 04MY fibre identity and 02FX give d2-1. Small cases checked: pair groupoid of A^1 and A^n, and group schemes (d1 = d2, excluded). No DAG node states 0461. The 5 declared tool_uses are generic algebra and are accepted. Batch 5: def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space is a general definition; the field-groupoid lemmas reach trf only through def-trf-algebraic-space; trf 056Y is a generic flatness criterion, not a trace-formula or Poincare step. All are OK. Maintainer note: blueprint.from.node is null, inherited from the creating delivery.
